Net: one dimension (dated BTC supply overhang vs imminent ETH ETF launch) leans ETH, ETH fundamentals lean mildly BTC, positioning slightly favors BTC on crowding — a small lean to Ether, near zero.

rows.rationale: Regime: both coins are in a macro-driven, risk-off deleveraging (Fear & Greed 11 Extreme Fear on 2026-02-28; VIX 19.86; Feb 5 tail-event crash per VanEck), but within crypto the tape is treating Ether as the higher-beta risk leg — VanEck's 2/5 note has BTC -2.88 sigma below its 200dma vs ETH -1.50 sigma, and 7-day declines of -22.2% BTC vs -29.7% ETH. Gold +30.7% over 120 days (5,248.90 USD) shows the scarce-money bid is intact and would favor BTC over ETH if it reasserts. ETH fundamentals deteriorate on all three network series: Ethereum TVL -41% (89.35B to 52.64B USD), daily fees -60.6% (21.96M to 8.65M USD), and — the price-independent read — ETH supply rising +464k ETH (+0.38%) over 180 days, so the burn is no longer shrinking supply. Positioning at the margin turns BTC-positive: BTC ETF flows flipped to +257.7M/+506.6M/+254.4M USD on Feb 24-26 after months of -200 to -800M days, while ETH ETF flows stayed mildly negative (-43.0M latest). What the market has already paid caps the score: eth_btc at 0.02934 is down from 0.03381 on Jan 1 and 0.0421 in Aug 2025, so BTC's recent outperformance is partly priced; funding_spread is -0.000017 (Ether longs are not the crowded side) and the dvol_spread (~+17 vol points, 72.38 vs 55.21) has compressed from ~21 in December. Two dimensions lean BTC, one leans ETH — a modest, not clean, long-BTC rating.

rows.rationale: All three dimensions lean Bitcoin, though none violently. (1) Regime: risk-off with a scarce-money bid — Fear & Greed printed 11 (Extreme Fear) on 2026-03-31 after two months in single digits/teens, VIX rose to 25.25 (+74% over Q1), Nasdaq -7.1% over Q1, while gold rose +18.9% over 180d to 4647.6 and DXY firmed to ~100. Web search dates the cause: a hawkish Fed hold on March 18 (PCE forecast raised to 2.7%), an oil/geopolitical shock, and an FTX distribution overhang. In that regime the higher-beta coin is the funding leg, and the Bitcoin-linked complex (COIN -54%, WGMI -27.7% over 180d) confirms broad crypto distress — mildly BTC-favorable. Stablecoin supply rising +4.5% to $313B is shared liquidity, neutral for the pair. (2) ETH fundamentals deteriorated hard: TVL -43.8% ($93.3B to $52.4B) and daily fees -44.2% ($20.4M to $11.4M) over 180d, while ETH supply is rising +0.39% (121.1M to 121.57M) — issuance outrunning the burn, so the scarcity story is absent. The Bitcoin-side hole is not empty: web search (Spotedcrypto via MEXC, 2026-03-24) reports Bitcoin exchange reserves at a 7-year low and record whale accumulation, holder-side evidence leaning the same way. (3) Positioning modestly BTC-favorable: BTC ETF flows recovered strongly in March (~+$1.3B month, incl. a 5-day $767M inflow streak per NeuralArB 2026-03-30) while ETH ETF flows stayed anemic (~-$50M in March). Funding spread +0.000027/8h is near zero — no meaningful crowding either way. The dvol spread of 20.12 vol points says options still price ETH as the risk asset. Anti-momentum caps the score: eth_btc 0.03083 is mid-range versus its 12m window (up +37.8% on the year so ETH outperformed on the year; down from the 0.042 Aug peak; but down from 0.0338 on Jan 1 so BTC outperformed in Q1 — both sides partially paid). With the fundamental damage largely priced after ETH fell ~56% below its August ATH, a clear-but-not-extreme BTC lean of +0.4.

rows.rationale: Three dimensions lean BTC, none strongly disagrees, so a moderate positive pair rating rather than a full one. ETH fundamental is the clearest pillar: Ethereum use is contracting (eth_tvl 52.4B, -43.8% over 180d; eth_fees 11.4M/day, -44.2%) and the supply question answers itself in ETH units — supply rose to 121.57M (+0.388% over 180d, +469,938 ETH), so fee burn is not offsetting issuance and the deflationary case is not running. Dollar-denominated TVL/fees partly track the price drawdown, but the supply series does not. Bitcoin has no matching activity series here; web search found only forward ETH catalysts (Glamsterdam targeted H1 2026, staking ETF access) with no delivered usage inflection in the window, so that side stays empty rather than bullish. Positioning also favors BTC: Q1 ETF flows were persistently negative for ETH (~-0.76B over Jan-Mar, including a 7-session outflow streak into late March) while BTC flows turned positive in March (+1.3B in Mar after a heavy January), each coin judged against its own history; funding_spread is slightly positive (+0.0000273/8h) so ETH longs are marginally the crowded side; dvol_spread +20.12 vol pts keeps ETH as the market's designated risk asset in a risk-off tape. Regime is mildly BTC-favorable within the pair but damaged for both: war-driven oil spike above $100, hawkish Fed hold (Mar 18, 2026 PCE revised 2.4%->2.7%), VIX 25.25 (+74% QTD), extreme fear at 11, and BTC dominance near cycle high (~60% per web) is the flight-to-quality signature. Anti-momentum caps the score from higher: ETH/BTC is +37.8% over 12 months (the market has paid for ETH on that window) but -9% over Q1 (it has also paid for BTC on that window) and +4.7% over 30 days after ETH's mid-March bounce — with mixed winner windows and the ratio already traveled, I stay at a lean-to-moderate BTC rating. Stablecoin supply near record (~313B, +4.5% 6m) is dry powder for both coins, not a differentiator.

Net: regime says market-cap book, ETH fundamentals lean the same way but weakly and with Bitcoin's side fee-soft, and the extreme paid relative move caps conviction — a modest Bitcoin lean of +0.2.

Cheapness at p4 plus a regime call both bind, so the score is a moderate lean toward the market-cap book rather than the +0.5 case: the anti-momentum cap is real and cheap Ether is not confirmed by any flow turn.

rows.rationale: Regime (primary, web-supported inside the window): the dated record shows a turn from Bitcoin leadership to Ether leadership. However, the regime is a mature one, not fresh: MEXC shows dominance falling 61.4% -> 59.94% in two weeks and labels the Bitcoin phase 'Complete' with Ethereum catch-up 'Current', and FX Empire flags a five-month falling wedge in ETH/BTC with a 0.0338 trigger. ETH fundamentals do not support the equal-weight side: fees/day latest 10.81M vs 30d avg 17.74M and 180d avg 19.46M, TVL 30d -19.0%, and bitrue.com (Nov 10, 2025) reports gas at ~0.067 Gwei with L1 earnings down ~99% from the early-October crash and L2 cannibalization; supply 121.25M with net issuance +78.56K over 30d means burn is not exceeding issuance. The one ETH-specific positive is OCC Interpretive Letter 1186 (Nov 18, 2025) letting national banks hold ETH for gas, but it is not confirmed by flows (ETH ETFs -$615M in Nov 2025 per MEXC; etf_flow 30d ETH -1706.0M vs BTC -4146.7M). What the market is already paying caps the Bitcoin lean: excess BTC-ETH is +4.7% (1m), +13.4% (3m), +12.3% (12m), so Bitcoin has already outperformed at three of four horizons and the anti-momentum rule caps rather than rewards that; the 6m horizon went the other way (-29.6%, Ether +15.3% vs BTC -14.3%), capping Ether there too. ETH/BTC at 0.0331 is p59 of a 0.0180-0.0421 window - not a cheap-Ether print that would argue for the equal-weight reset, but also not a deep-discount entry for more Bitcoin. Funding spread +0.03bp (30d ann. -0.3%) is noise; DVOL spread 23.4 (ETH 72.2 vs BTC 48.8) is the equal-weight book's extra bump in a drawdown and argues against leaning Ether into this tape. Fear & Greed 28 with both coins -17% to -22% over 1m is a soft but not disorderly backdrop. Net: one dimension (regime, web-supported) leans market-cap, one (ETH fundamentals) supports Bitcoin by absence of an Ether case but has a soft Bitcoin network counterpart (BTC fees ~$300k/day, a 12-month low per theblock.co), and the positioning dimension pulls back toward zero. That mix is a +0.2 lean to the market-cap book, not a clear case.

rows.rationale: Regime is the anchor and it points to the market-cap book: a dated web record inside the window (fxempire.com, Nov 2025) states 'Bitcoin's macro leadership remains intact,' and ETH/BTC sits at a multi-year low (0.031-0.032 as of Nov 24, 2025 per blog.mexc.com) with the pair ratio at 0.0331 on 2025-11-30 — Ether remains the small sleeve rather than having run. The ETH-fundamental pillar agrees on the bearish-for-ETH side: TVL 68.28B is -19.0% over 30d, daily fees 10.81M run below both the 30d (17.74M) and 180d (19.46M) averages, and supply is expanding (+78.56K net issuance 30d, +448.67K 180d), so there is no burn-driven tightening story supporting an Ether-led window. However, the third pillar caps the lean rather than extending it: Bitcoin has already outperformed by +4.7% 1m, +13.4% 3m, +12.3% 12m, and the ratio has already fallen -5.7% 1m / -16.2% 3m — that performance is paid, and the anti-momentum rule bars scoring the leader higher on trend alone. Countervailing Ether-specific items inside the window pull back further toward zero: OCC Interpretive Letter 1186 (Nov 18, 2025) lets U.S. national banks hold ETH for gas fees with no BTC analogue, and Bitcoin's share is falling (dominance 61.4% early Nov -> 59.94% Nov 24), the wrong direction for the strict 'share rising' branch. On the other side, Bitcoin's ETF 30d outflow of -4146.7M (2.4x Ether's -1706.0M) is the largest negative in the pack, Ether carries a 23.4-pt DVOL premium that is a cost of leaning to Ether in a drawdown where Ether's 365d max drawdown is -63.3% vs Bitcoin's -32.1%, and funding is symmetric (+0.03 bp Ether-Bitcoin spread). Net: one clear dimension (dated regime record) plus weak ETH usage/supply support the market-cap book, while paid-in performance, falling dominance, and the fresh Ether policy catalyst keep the lean modest at +0.25. Update tier shows no confirmed turn (forex.com: Ether reclaiming its 200-day MA is 'still tentative'), so nothing justifies a larger Bitcoin lean.

rows.rationale: Regime (primary, outweighs): dated web results inside the window put the tape Bitcoin-led with Ether as the small sleeve — zipmex.com (Feb 2026) has BTC dominance near 58-59% after Bitcoin's ~50% correction from its Oct-2025 ATH of $126,210; Bloomberg via finance.yahoo.com has Bitcoin holding ~60% of the $2.35T market while Ether has dropped to ~10%, and dates the leadership gap directly ('Ether has stumbled almost 60% since its peak in August, while Bitcoin is down roughly 45%'). coinbird.com reads Bitcoin 56.41% vs Ethereum 9.83% (~85/15 on a two-coin basis), and advisorperspectives.com in the last 7d states 'bitcoin is in the lead.' That is the case for the market-cap book. ETH fundamentals corroborate rather than contradict: TVL 52.64B, -26.1% at 30d and -41.1% at 180d; fees/day 8.65M vs a 30d average of 13.19M and 180d average of 17.15M; supply 121.49M with net issuance +78.44K at 30d and +464.33K at 180d — burn did not exceed issuance. Forbes dates the cause: post-Dencun, L2s pay reduced fees to mainnet so 'network usage is increasing while the burn on the mainnet is decreasing'; Yahoo/Glassnode puts ETH fees at their lowest since 2017. What the market is already paying pulls the call back toward zero: the Bitcoin-minus-Ether excess is +9.5% at 1m, +8.4% at 3m and +15.8% at 6m, so Bitcoin's lead is already in the tape and caps Bitcoin; ETH/BTC is 0.0293 at p42 of its 0.0180-0.0421 window (-12.0% 1m, -25.7% 6m but +13.9% 12m), mid-range rather than a capitulation print; and the 12m ex-last-1m excess of -28.9% shows the prior year was Ether-led, so February is a reversal inside a longer Ether trend. Funding spread -0.17 bp (30d ann. -2.5%) with Ether at -0.50 bp is a faint washed-out-ETH contrarian pull. Both books are in deep drawdown (Fear & Greed 11, 30d -15; max 365d drawdown BTC -49.7% vs ETH -62.3%; ETF 30d flows BTC -1534.1M, ETH -778.4M), and DVOL spread of 17.2 is the extra bump of an Ether lean in this tape. Net: regime plus weak Ether activity favor the market-cap book, but the paid-in 1m/3m/6m excess and mid-window ratio keep the score at a moderate lean rather than a strong one.

rows.rationale: Regime is the primary pillar and it is decisively Bitcoin-led per dated web results inside the window: Bloomberg/Yahoo puts Bitcoin at ~60% of the $2.35T market cap while Ether is ~10%, coinbird shows 55.46%/9.73% (Bitcoin ~85% of the two coins), zipmex has BTC dominance 58-59% with investors 'favoring the relative safety of Bitcoin', and the 7-day advisorperspectives piece states flatly 'bitcoin is in the lead.' Per the strategy rules the regime outweighs the other dimensions when a web result dated inside the window supports it, so the lean is toward the market-cap book. The second dimension agrees directionally but is one-sided: Ether's own network series are deteriorating (TVL −26.1% 30d / −41.1% 180d, fees 8.65M/day vs a 17.15M 180d average, supply +464.33K over 180d = net issuance), and the Forbes-dated Dencun finding explains why — L2 fee reimbursement to mainnet collapsed so the burn rate 'has sharply declined', structurally impairing the ETH supply thesis. This pack has no Bitcoin network activity/supply counterpart, so this is evidence about Ether's weakness rather than a finished comparison, and it only reinforces rather than drives the call. The third dimension pulls back toward zero: Bitcoin has already been paid in the window — excess returns +9.5% 1m / +8.4% 3m / +15.8% 6m — which caps the Bitcoin side under anti-momentum, and ETH/BTC at 0.0293 sits at p42 of its 0.0180-0.0421 window, mid-range rather than an extreme that would cap Ether further. The cycle horizon also cuts the other way (12m ex-last-1m −28.9% means Ether was the prior-year winner now giving it back). Positioning is symmetric: both ETF books in outflow (Bitcoin −1534.1mn/30d, Ether −778.4mn/30d) with modest 7d reversals, and funding spreads mildly negative (−0.17bp, −2.5% ann.) so neither side is crowded. The DVOL spread of 17.2 (+4.0 30d) is an extra bump for the equal-weight book in a Fear&Greed-11 drawdown, a modest cost of leaning Ether. Net: a clear regime-led lean to Bitcoin, held well short of a strong score by the already-paid excess returns and the mid-range ratio.

Funding is flat (spread +0.27bp latest), so no crowding; DVOL spread 20.1 is near the upper half of its 13.0–37.8 range, an added cost of leaning Ether. ETF flows favor Bitcoin (BTC 30d +1315.6M vs ETH 30d −45.8M and negative on 7d/30d/90d) but BTC's own 30d reverses sign on 7d (−202.1M) and 90d (−495.8M), and openpr/eth-spot-ETF reports conflict. Net: one dimension (regime, dated) supports Bitcoin, ETH fundamentals mildly reinforce, while the 'already paid' dimension is mixed across horizons and caps conviction — a lean to the market-cap book, not a clear case.

rows.rationale: Three dimensions pull in different directions and the result is a small Ether lean, close to zero. (1) Regime: dated in-window results say the tape is Ether-led — bitget (week of Aug 26, 2026) has 'ETH gained nearly 29% in seven days, outpacing Bitcoin's 23% weekly advance' and CoinDesk (last 7d) dates Ether's leadership from early June with 'the pair has rallied 25% since the June 6 bottom' plus a golden cross on ETH/BTC. That is the primary pillar and it points at the equal-weight book. The share counter-print is only a one-session drift: TokenPost's Tuesday snapshot has Bitcoin dominance 58.76% (+0.12pp) vs Ethereum 10.32% (−0.01pp) — 'leadership narrowing toward Bitcoin' — too thin to overturn the dated trend. (2) ETH fundamental: mixed and therefore neutral-to-weak support for Ether. TVL 48.77B is +18.9% over 30d, a strong month, but the supply side is not burning: supply 122.00M with +86.55K net issuance over 30d (+495.85K over 180d), corroborated in-window by 'Ethereum Supply Rises by 20,125 ETH in a Week, Breaking Post-Merge Trend' and CoinOTAG's blob-fee burn of only ~0.22 ETH over seven days against 0.85% annual supply growth. Fees flat at 9.56M/day 30d vs 10.30M/day 180d. Bitcoin's side is not empty: Glassnode via gncrypto/CryptoSlate dates fees at 0.69–0.70% of miner revenue (lowest in 10 years) and hash rate down ~33% since Oct 2025 — a dated erosion of Bitcoin's economics that weighs against the market-cap book. (3) What is already paid: this is the cap. ETH/BTC 0.0314 (p55 of 0.0258–0.0406) has risen +6.9% over 1m and +12.7% over 3m, and the excess column shows Ether already outperforming at 1m (−8.7%), 3m (−15.0%) and 6m (−7.9%). CoinDesk itself dates the move at +25% off the June 6 low and warns prior ETH/BTC golden crosses (May 2022, Aug 2022, Jul 2025) were bull traps or reversed within four weeks. Leaning harder into Ether here would be leaning on paid-for outperformance, and the equal-weight reset sells that winner. The 12m still favors Bitcoin (+14.7% excess, ratio −20.5%) which keeps the score from going further negative. Positioning is split (BTC 30d ETF +3539.1M vs ETH +1851.5M, but 90d ETH +1823.2M vs BTC +205.1M), funding spread is only −0.08bp (30d avg), and the ETH−BTC DVOL spread of 13.7 marks the equal-weight book as the bumpier one in a sentiment tape that already ran (Fear & Greed 62, +35 in 30d). Net: a mild −0.15 lean to the equal-weight book on the dated regime, heavily dampened by the paid-for ratio move and ETH supply inflation.

Regime is split on dated evidence: Ether leads on performance (ETH +~29% vs BTC +23% over seven days per the week-of-Aug-26 Coin Edition piece; 'Ethereum Leads' a rebound +17.7% vs +10.2% on cryptotimes.io), but Bitcoin holds and is gaining share ('Bitcoin dominance rose to 58.76% (+0.12pp), while Ethereum's share slipped to 10.32%', TokenPost Tuesday; 'Bitcoin still controls nearly three-fifths of total capitalization', Coin Edition). The equal-weight book's premise requires Ether gaining AND the relative price not having paid; relative has already paid (ETH/BTC +6.9% 1m, +12.7% 3m, +7.3% 6m; CoinDesk: 'The pair has rallied 25% since the June 6 bottom'), so anti-momentum caps the Ether lean and the equal-weight reset would sell the already-run coin. But the Bitcoin side has its own structural gap: 'Transaction fees now account for 0.69% of miner revenue, the lowest share in 10 years' with hash rate 'fallen about 33% since October 2025' (gncrypto/TradingView) — so ETH's weakness is partly matched. Positioning is nearly symmetric (funding 30d ann. BTC +6.5% vs ETH +5.6%, spread -0.9% favouring less-crowded Ether longs; ETF 30d +3539.1M BTC vs +1851.5M ETH, both heavily bid). Policy is coin-symmetric (Cboe 3x BTC/ETH ETF filing Aug 10-14; Thailand SEC passive BTC-or-ETH ETF consultation Aug 21-24). Net: no cross-coin edge from the fundamentals or pricing; the only live, uncapped signal is Bitcoin's rising share of the two coins, which justifies a small positive score rather than zero.
